candidate.answerReason: The tangent and radius form a right triangle, giving the center distance 5r/3. The nearest circle point is 5r/3-r=2r/3=l/2 from A.

methods.label: Find the center distance, then subtract the radius
methods.explanation:
Let \(O\) be the circle's center and \(T\) the point of tangency. The radius \(OT\) is perpendicular to the tangent segment \(AT\), so triangle \(AOT\) is right. Here \(OT=r>0\) and \(AT=l=4r/3\). The Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
AO^2=r^2+\left(\frac{4r}{3}\right)^2
=\frac{25r^2}{9}.
\]
Taking the positive length, \(AO=5r/3>r\), so \(A\) is outside the circle.

The closest circle point is the point \(P\) on segment \(AO\) with \(OP=r\). To see why, take any point \(X\) on the circle. The route from \(A\) through \(X\) to \(O\) cannot be shorter than the straight segment \(AO\), so
\[
AX+r\ge AO,
\qquad AX\ge AO-r.
\]
Point \(P\) attains this bound. Hence the shortest distance is
\[
AP=AO-r=\frac{5r}{3}-r
=\frac{2r}{3}=\frac l2.
\]
The answer is \(\dfrac12l\), choice C.
